combat_history.event: Deployed to the Tibetan plateau during the China–India border standoff.
combat_history.significance: Showcased rapid wheeled fires where heavy tracked guns struggle.

modernization.description: Replacing towed/older guns at scale; digitised fire control.
modernization.impact: Modernises and mobilises PLA fire support broadly.

vulnerabilities.description: Less off-road mobility than tracked SPGs.
Vulnerable if it does not displace quickly.
vulnerabilities.context: Modern sensors locate firing positions fast.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Rapidly-deployable mobile fire support, especially in plateau and road-connected terrain.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Light/medium combined-arms brigades; complements tracked PLZ-05.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: PLZ-05 is the tracked heavy SPG; the PCL-181 is the lighter, road-mobile wheeled gun.
The French truck-mounted 155 mm gun pioneered this mobile-artillery concept the PCL-181 shares.
The K9 is a tracked premium SPG; the PCL-181 emphasises wheeled mobility and cost.

doctrine.role: Wheeled, rapidly-deployable 155 mm truck howitzer — a mobile fire-support mainstay.
doctrine.employment: Self-deploys over roads, fires and displaces in minutes; networked digital fire control.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Mobility, affordability and producibility over cross-country performance.
doctrine.threat_context: Fields mobile fires at scale across difficult terrain like the Indian border.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the tracked PLZ-05, France's CAESAR and Korea's K9.

curated_sources.title: IISS Military Balance — China land forces
